prompt: hpx::future destructor blocking behavior vs std::future
answer:
`hpx::future` destructors do not block, even when the future was created by `hpx::async` and `.get()` or `.wait()` was not called. HPX deliberately diverges from the standard in this respect so that all HPX futures have the same semantics, regardless of how they were created. [P0701R1; HPX PR #3205]

`std::future` destructors generally do not block, except for a `std::future` returned by `std::async` with an asynchronous task that is still running and whose future is the last reference to the shared state. In that case, destruction blocks until the task completes. The same exception applies to the last `std::shared_future`. [Microsoft Learn; P0701R1]

| Future type | Destructor behavior |
|---|---|
| `hpx::future` | Never blocks |
| `std::future` from `std::promise` or `std::packaged_task` | Does not block |
| `std::future` from `std::async`, unfinished asynchronous task | Blocks until completion |
| `std::shared_future` from `std::async`, last reference and task unfinished | Blocks until completion |
